rows.description: A young child asked "was the man wearing a red hat?" later remembers a red hat that was never there; adults' wording in questions can seed false details in a child's memory.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child's memory of a trip blends with what siblings and parents have said about it since, until they cannot tell what they saw from what they were told.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Witnessing an event and then reading reports [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult who saw a minor accident adds details from later news and chat messages and feels fully certain, since confident recall is not proof of accuracy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.subtype: Asking open questions and noting memory early [Observer]
rows.description: A teacher or parent gathering a child's account asks "what happened?" rather than suggesting details, and records the account soon; memory is rebuilt each time and shaped by questions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: An adult in a dispute says "this is how I remember it" instead of "this is what happened", and looks for a message or photo, since confident memory can still be wrong.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager shrugs off a flood or cyclone warning because nothing bad has happened before, and keeps scrolling, feeling safe because the world so far has been ordinary.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A family under a real warning pauses to pack and gather things, sure it will pass; the mind clings to the usual pattern and underestimates how fast conditions can change.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Colleagues stay put when the alarm rings [Observer]
rows.description: An employee sees coworkers keep working through a fire alarm, each looking at the others for cues; nobody moves until someone does.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An adult notes exits, keeps a small emergency kit, follows official warnings without waiting for proof, and prefers the mild embarrassment of a false alarm over being late.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child believes a "fact" about food or ghosts because everyone repeats it; hearing it often makes it feel familiar, and familiar feels true.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
